title: Snapmaker Orca · U1 print popup + multiACE
summary: Route C: a plate sliced for a U1 with an ACE-fed toolhead is rewritten in Orca after export, so the gcode names physical heads and the bays that feed them. The plan now keeps Orca's own filament-to-toolhead assignment whenever it costs the same, and the bay can be re-chosen from the print popup without slicing anything again.

features.why: Reads the exported gcode, plans each filament's (head, bay), and writes a sibling file the machine can run: physical T numbers, an ACE_SWAP_HEAD where a head must present another bay, purge stamps, a preload block before the prime line, and the `; multiACE plan:` header the popup and the bridge already read. Ported from multiACE's own preflight at tag v0.99.8b, behaviour not code.

features.what: One hook, and a sibling file rather than an in-place rewrite
features.why: It runs straight after export, on the file the U1 send zips and Ctrl+G packages. Writing beside the temp gcode leaves the preview mapping the logical file, makes a re-map a re-run rather than a re-export, and keeps multiACE's own rewriter runnable over the same input to measure drift - which is 0 differing lines.

features.what: Orca's own filament assignment wins a tie
features.why: The optimiser minimises swaps and is silent about everything else, so among equal-cost plans it took an arbitrary one - on a four-colour plate it moved all four filaments for no gain. The identity is now priced and kept when it ties.

features.what: The ACE bay can be re-chosen from the popup, for nothing
features.why: A filament's toolhead IS the tool number, so moving it re-exports the file; its bay is one argument on each swap line. `sw_SetAceBays` re-runs the rewriter over the same logical gcode, and the panel offers `Use the bays they are in` only when re-addressing would clear EVERY bay.

features.what: Two pre-existing defects fixed on the way
features.why: The send zip was named by display name alone and reused whenever it existed, so a resend after a re-slice could ship the previous bytes with a checksum that could not tell; it is keyed to its source and stamped now. And nothing refused a SET_PRINT_EXTRUDER_MAP that moves a tool off its own head on an ACE plate.

verify: Slice a multi-filament plate with Toolhead 4 set to `ACE - 4 slots` / `ACE 1`. A `.ace.gcode` sibling appears beside the plate's temp gcode in the project backup.
The post-slice notification names the swap count and the purge.
Set Toolhead 4 back to `Stock feeder` and re-slice: the sibling is gone and the plate is untouched.
Send the ACE plate: the popup draws toolhead boxes with bay addresses, not four cards.
With a bay holding another spool, Send is refused; if every spool the plate wants is in the unit, `Use the bays they are in` clears it without re-slicing.
Export G-code and `grep -c ACE_SWAP_HEAD` the result.
checks: libslic3r: 260 assertions in 16 cases `[ace_mmu_rewrite]`, plus `[ace_mmu]` 191 and `[ace_mmu_plan]` 140
Drift against multiACE v0.99.8b's own rewriter: 0 differing lines on all three fixtures
Simulator: bay-fix 16/16, ACE dialog 18/18, print dialog 52/52, Device page 99/99
Real U1 811002511261022618B3, read-only: 15/15 with Test_Cube_PLA_4h15m, 15/15 with ChickenPark, 17/17 with the multiACE plate
open: No print has been run past its first seconds with the ACE half engaged. Everything on hardware so far is read-only.
Combined (`multi`) ACE mode is refused with a message: the emitter's slot -> (unit, bay) map is not written, and the page has never been driven in that mode either.
Two heads sharing one ACE unit is refused - the planner counts that unit's capacity twice.

The bay re-map is offered only when it would clear every bay. When a colour the plate wants is in no bay at all, the panel still cannot say which bay to put it in: writing a bay's identity (`ACE_SPOOL_ASSIGN`) is unbuilt.
Whether the stock pre-extrude macro accepts `FORCE=1` on this firmware is unverified, so the rewriter emits the plain form the hardware-verified reference file used.
